title: Slow to Grind Enough Beans for 12-Cup Drip Coffee Maker
text:
Slow to Grind Enough Beans for 12-Cup Drip Coffee Maker. This SECURA AUTOMATIC COFFEE GRINDER AND SPICE GRINDER (2.5 Ounce Capacity, Silver) works on the same principle as my tried-and-true KitchenAid coffee grinder. (That grinder has been grinding away for over 20 years--I don’t know why KitchenAid stopped making this great appliance.) Basically, you put your beans or seeds into the bladed stainless steel bowl, add the plastic lid, add the square plastic cover, and press down on the square cover in 8-second bursts to grind the stuff in the bowl.

An 8-second burst grinds 2 tablespoons of coffee beans to the equivalent of a “percolator” grind. This is too coarse a grind for my Hamilton Beach Coffeemaker, so my beans need additional 8-second bursts. Given that my ancient KitchenAid appliance grinds 8 tablespoons of coffee beans to the equivalent of a “drip” grind in just 10 seconds, the Secura grinder won’t be replacing it.

Another reason NOT to embrace the Secura grinder is that the bladed bowl doesn’t hold enough coffee beans at one time for 10-12 cups of coffee. The “Max Fill” line only accommodates the beans for about 6 cups of coffee. For 12 cups of coffee, you have to fill the bladed bowl twice, and grind each time in at least two 8-second bursts. If you don’t grind in short bursts, the grinder will overheat and shut down--and require a 45-minute cooldown.

Finally, the plastic lid that goes onto the bladed stainless steel bowl fits very tightly. It is quite difficult to remove. This is a major drawback when you’re opening a container of finely ground coffee beans or seeds.

The grinder bowl, plastic lid, and square plastic cover are all dishwasher safe, but hand washing is recommended. A reason to follow this recommendation is that plastic becomes cloudy if it’s subjected to high dishwasher temperatures.

I can use this grinder for spices, but I don’t grind a lot of spices, except for nutmeg. For nutmeg, I use a specialized nutmeg grinder that looks like a peppermill, so that the nutmeg is always freshly ground.

Stainless steel blade and stainless steel exterior. Durability and powerful performance.
